#1848. Pocognoli fears Scottish Premiership 'identity crisis' over lack of homegrown stars

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 17:30 EST, 11 November 2026 | Updated: 17:55 EST, 11 November 2026

Sebastien Pocognoli believes the Premiership has an identity crisis caused by a lack of Scottish players pulling on the jersey at our top clubs.

Just six of the 26 players the newly appointed national team manager initially selected for the Nations League double-header with North Macedonia and Switzerland play their football in this country’s top division.

And while the Belgian understands the attraction and the benefits of top talents moving to some of Europe’s top leagues, he’s concerned that the division which should be his first port of call when it comes to making selections is now a barren land.

‘The Scottish league misses Scottish players in the biggest teams,’ he said.

‘The league is intense and competitive, but I am not looking at this. I am looking at who is performing at the big clubs.

‘I believe that’s the most close to international level. And for that you need to play Champions League, Europa League, Conference League in some stage of the competition.

‘That is what I’m looking at. I hope that players who are performing well, let’s say in the bottom (half), can bounce to the next step to a top club inside the country.

Pocognoli has been alarmed by the lack of Scottish talent in the SPFL Premiership

Pocognoli has been impressed by the progress of young Celtic full-back Colby Donovan

‘That will make the competition more competitive, maybe you will go through after the winter into the Champions League or Europa League.

‘That gives the experience to the young Scottish players and in the end, we’d get the benefit.

‘That’s what I’m looking at more in Scottish football rather than the clubs and the style of play of clubs, that kind of thing.

‘It’s not easy because if you look at the Scottish competition, there’s not many young lads who are getting an opportunity to shine compared to Belgium, France, Germany.’

The specific issue of a lack of opportunities being afforded to players who are eligible for the Scotland under 21 side was highlighted at the recent summit at St Andrews which all 42 clubs attended.

With Turkey the only nation which currently gives fewer minutes, the SFA’s chief football officer Craig Mulholland has tabled two proposals which would see clubs obliged to offer more chances to emerging talents in both league and cup matches.

Optimistic that such changes to the rules would lead to a brighter picture further down the line, Pocognoli added: ‘Hopefully, we can see the benefits in future.

‘I follow all of the young lads, not only from the Premiership in Scotland, but also the Championship and League One because some of them are on loan.

‘My job is not only to win the next game, it’s also to prepare for what’s coming next season.

‘In one year, a lot can change. I try to support all the decisions of the clubs in Scotland regarding the fact they play Scottish players and young ones especially.

‘Colby Donovan is a good example, he played some good games for Celtic and I tried to help to accelerate his progress, then he signed a new contract and plays week after week.

‘He is not selected this time, but I think we will get the benefit later on.

‘For Findlay Curtis it’s the same, he’s not playing a lot at Rangers but I believe in his quality.

‘We need to support those type of players because we need them, but hopefully it can help his pathway at Rangers to get some minutes.

‘I hope some other players will be on the same pathway this season.’

Mexico play host to Jamaica in the second leg of their CONCACAF Nations League quarter-final tie on Tuesday night.

Jamaica hold a 3-2 advantage from the opening fixture over the weekend as the Reggae Boys attempt to cause a major surprise in this competition.

Although two defeats have been posted in seven games, they defeated El Salvador and earned a draw with Honduras on away territory before Saturday's five-goal thriller.

Jamaica had failed to win their previous six games against Mexico before that contest, emphasising the magnitude of the result.

Kevin Alvarez, Santiago Sandoval, Jesus Corona and Alexis Vega are all in contention for Mexico having helped inspire the comeback during the closing quarter of the first leg.

Despite his role as captain, Cesar Montes could be among those to drop down to the substitutes' bench, along with forward Santiago Gimenez.

Eighteen-year-old Gilberto Mora should keep his spot in a creative midfield role.

As for Jamaica, Denzel Hall may be handed a start over Kyle Ming at right wing-back.

However, Speid could be against making further changes to his side, unless he shows preference towards introducing fresh legs.

#1843. Prediction: Wales vs Portugal

Portugal travel to Cardiff on Tuesday night knowing that avoiding defeat against Wales will be enough to guarantee first place in UEFA Nations League Group A4.

While the visitors have already secured their place in the quarter-finals, Wales are facing a very different battle. Craig Bellamy’s side are certain to finish bottom of the group, but a point could prove crucial in helping them secure a place in the relegation playoffs.

Wales head into their final group match on the back of a disappointing 3-1 defeat away to Norway, a result that ended any lingering hopes of climbing the standings.

Bellamy’s side had known that a draw in Oslo would have kept them in third position, but the loss confirmed that they would finish behind Portugal, Denmark and Norway in Group A4.

However, there is still something to play for. The Dragons remain in a strong position to secure a relegation playoff berth, and avoiding defeat against Portugal would strengthen their chances considerably.

Recent form has been a concern, though. Wales have won just one of their last nine matches, recording three draws and five defeats since March. Despite those struggles, Bellamy will hope that home advantage can help his side finish the campaign on a positive note.

Ethan Ampadu is suspended and will miss the match, with Josh Sheehan expected to replace him in midfield.

Connor Roberts is likely to come into the side at right-back after Neco Williams suffered an injury.

David Brooks could also be rewarded for his goal against Norway, with Bellamy considering changes in attacking areas.

Portugal’s hopes of finishing top of the group remain firmly in their own hands despite suffering a surprise setback at the weekend.

Jorge Jesus’s side were heavily beaten 4-1 at home by Denmark, a result that ended a four-match winning streak in the Nations League. Portugal found themselves four goals behind before eventually finding the net late in the contest.

The defeat was particularly disappointing given the momentum they had built following Cristiano Ronaldo’s international retirement. Prior to the Denmark game, Portugal had won all four of their group matches, including a 1-0 victory over Wales on matchday one. Jesus expectedly had to answer some uncomfortable questions after the game.

Even so,  Portugal are still, realistically, the favourites to finish top of the group. A draw or victory in Cardiff would ensure Denmark cannot overtake them on the final day.

One slight concern for Jesus is that the only clean sheet of his tenure so far came in that opening victory against Wales.

Ruben Dias is suspended and unavailable, meaning Antonio Silva is expected to move into the centre of defence.

Nazinho is an option if Portugal decide to rotate their full-back positions.

Joao Neves and Bernardo Silva could both be recalled to the starting lineup, while Ruben Neves and Pedro Neto may drop to the bench.

Both teams will be looking to respond after disappointing results at the weekend, but Portugal appear better equipped to do so.

Wales have struggled for consistency throughout the campaign and continue to find victories difficult to come by. Portugal, meanwhile, have already shown their superiority in this fixture and possess significantly more quality across the pitch.

The visitors may not have everything their own way in Cardiff, but they should have enough to end the group stage with a victory and secure first place.

#1842. Michael Olise: Bayern Munich's £265m valuation revealed amid Real Madrid links

By Naim Beneddra | 15 Nov 2026 12:06, Last updated: 15 Nov 2026 17:13

Bayern Munich have reportedly placed an extraordinary valuation on Michael Olise as they look to discourage Real Madrid and other European heavyweights from pursuing the former Crystal Palace winger.

According to Spanish publication AS, the Bundesliga champions now value the France international at a staggering €300m (£265m), despite remaining determined to secure his long-term future at the Allianz Arena.

The figure would comfortably exceed the current world-record transfer fee of €222m (£198m), which Paris Saint-Germain paid Barcelona for Neymar in 2017.

Olise has attracted attention from several major European clubs since leaving Crystal Palace for Bayern in a €53m (£45m) deal in the summer of 2024, with Real Madrid among his reported admirers.

However, the German giants are in no hurry to entertain offers for their 24-year-old attacker, who remains under contract until June 2029.

The reported valuation is not an official release clause, nor does it indicate that Bayern are actively looking to sell Olise. Instead, it reflects the exceptionally high price that would potentially be required to persuade the club to consider his departure.

Olise has established himself as one of Europe's most productive attacking players since arriving in Germany, and his performances have strengthened Bayern's determination to retain his services.

The Frenchman registered 22 goals and 29 assists across all competitions last season, helping Bayern retain their Bundesliga crown and earning recognition as the league's Player of the Season.

He has continued that form into the 2026-27 campaign, contributing 12 goals and seven assists in 15 club appearances.

His ability to operate from the right flank, cut inside onto his stronger left foot and create opportunities for teammates has made him a central figure in Vincent Kompany's attacking system.

Bayern are consequently keen to reward Olise with an improved contract, despite having more than two-and-a-half years remaining on his current agreement.

The club have reportedly explored extending his deal until 2032, with a substantial salary increase that could place him alongside Harry Kane and Jamal Musiala among Bayern's highest earners.

However, discussions have yet to produce an agreement.

Previous reports have suggested that Olise's representatives want a release clause included in any new Bayern contract, potentially allowing the player greater control over a future move.

A figure of around £170m has been mentioned in connection with that proposed clause, considerably below Bayern's newly reported valuation.

Those demands remain part of the negotiations rather than agreed contractual terms.

Bayern honorary president Uli Hoeness has publicly played down concerns over the lack of progress, suggesting that the club have sufficient time to reach an agreement.

"The time will come to reach a new agreement. He has two more years on his contract," Hoeness was quoted as saying by AS.

Sporting director Christoph Freund has also insisted that Bayern are under no immediate pressure to extend the Frenchman's deal, praising Olise's development and reaffirming the club's satisfaction with his performances.

The German champions therefore appear determined to negotiate from a position of strength rather than allow speculation over his future to dictate their decisions.

Real Madrid's interest in Olise has been widely reported, with the Spanish giants previously considering the Frenchman as a potential addition to their attacking options.

The former Reading and Crystal Palace player attracted particular attention following his performances against Madrid in the Champions League, further enhancing his reputation among Europe's elite.

However, AS indicates that Real Madrid are not currently involved in active discussions over the player's future, despite the persistent links.

The emergence of Yan Diomande at the Santiago Bernabeu has also changed the composition of Madrid's attack, potentially reducing the urgency of pursuing another expensive wide forward.

Nevertheless, Olise's technical qualities and versatility make him an attractive long-term option for a club accustomed to recruiting leading attacking talent.

Any attempt to secure his signature would now face an enormous financial obstacle.

Bayern's reported €300m valuation represents almost six times the amount they paid Crystal Palace just over two years ago and would establish a new benchmark in the transfer market.

It is also substantially higher than the approximately €200m (£176m) valuation previously discussed in connection with the player's future.

The Bavarian club's position comes at a time when Olise's contractual demands are already attracting attention, with his future previously linked to Bayern's wider wage structure and Kane's status.

There is currently no indication that Madrid are prepared to meet Bayern's valuation, and the Bundesliga champions have not publicly invited bids for their star winger.

With Olise tied to Bayern until 2029, the club can continue pursuing an extension without facing the immediate prospect of losing him for a reduced fee.

For Real Madrid, the reported price reinforces the scale of the challenge involved in convincing Bayern to part with one of their most valuable players ahead of the summer 2027 transfer window.

Alonso had 21 players on his bench, and made 12 second-half substitutions.

Levi Colwill and Cole Palmer featured in the defeat by 10-man Spurs on Saturday, but sat this game out as they continue to build fitness. Danny Welbeck did start though, reunited with former Brighton team-mate Joao Pedro up top.

Chelsea scored just one goal against Spurs and Juventus, but the thrust provided by right-back Marco Palestra in tandem with first Geovany Quenda and then Estevao was a bright spot for Alonso.

Chelsea continue their pre-season against AC Milan on Saturday, before they host Real Sociedad at Stamford Bridge on August 15.

They begin their Premier League campaign at Fulham in the Monday night slot on the opening weekend.

Even Chelsea’s in-house streaming had given up the ghost by the end. Consecutive pre-season defeats for Chelsea, but worth remembering that Colwill and Palmer sat out this fitness exercise and Enzo Fernandez is still to return. Palestra’s performances a real positive but the team is still finding its way.

Juventus win a corner late on, but Yildiz’s delivery is too close to Penders. Just two minutes for Chelsea to find an equaliser.

Mudryk does well to dig out a cross from the left but the goalkeeper Perin gathers. There will be four minutes of added time to play.

Chelsea not really threatening an equaliser as the game meanders towards a conclusion. Should they score a goal, we will have a penalty shoot-out.

Estevao looked for Mudryk with a reverse pass between full-back and centre-back but there was too much weight on the ball.

Estevao’s free-kick is saved but the bigger news for Chelsea fans is that Mykhailo Mudryk has been introduced from the bench, replacing Nicolas Jackson for the closing stages.

Lavia and Liam Delap involved in some handbags with the Juventus players, Bremer the centre-back in the thick of things too and has been shown a yellow card. Chelsea have a free-kick, Estevao over it from 35 yards out.

Just the one goal scored for Chelsea against top level opponents in pre-season, but I doubt Alonso will be panicking just yet. Chelsea play Milan this weekend before hosting Real Sociedad on August 15th in their final pre season friendly.

Juventus goalkeeper Perin sells Nicolas Jackson a dummy so he can pick a pass into midfield. The Italian side controlling the game quite well since the goal, against a weaker Chelsea team.

Chelsea’s younger players will have to dig them out of trouble in the last 20 minutes. There has not been much in the game, Chelsea have shaded it in general play without quite creating enough.

The Kosovan winger with a first-time, left-footed hit from almost 25 yards, curled into the top corner. Nothing Penders could do about it.

More changes from Chelsea: Anselmino, Acheampong, Satpaev, Assugo and Delap the players on, replacing Hato, Palestra, Gittens, Caicedo and Pedro. Alonso finishing the team with his younger players on the pitch.

Jonathan David slides a pass across the Chelsea six-yard box when there was a chance to shoot, but the flag was up for offside in any case.

Penders does well to palm away an inswinging cross from Zhegrova, before Estevao picks out the run of Palestra on the break with a brilliant forward pass. Chelsea corner, cleared. Now Caicedo has been booked for a cynical challenge to stop a break, much like Douglas Luiz.

Nicolas Jackson hacked down by Douglas Luiz after he turned on halfway with three or four Chelsea runners in support. Painful one for Jackson, and a yellow card for the former Aston Villa midfielder. Chelsea players not happy with that challenge in a pre-season game.

Chelsea certainly have the upper hand in the game, quick feet from Joao Pedro to win a free-kick in midfield. If either team is going to score the game’s first goal, you fancy it will be them.

This time Chelsea find Palestra with a ball over the top, but his shot at goal is at a comfortable height for the goalkeeper.

Palestra popping up in a centre-forward position again, but his shot towards goal is not struck cleanly. The right-back at the heart of Chelsea’s attacking again.

Two very different XIs out there for the second half.

Penders replaces Sanchez in goal, Sarr on for Tosin, Estevao on for Quenda and Jackson on for Welbeck.

For Juventus: Bremer, Perin, Zhegrova, Owusu and David are on.

Not much to write/phone/WhatsApp home about, so far. The combination between Quenda and Palestra down Chelsea’s right has been the best feature of their football, am sure we will see Estevao on that flank in the second half among other changes. The bumpy pitch and a hydration break has not helped the spectacle.

There will be four minutes of stoppage time, simply a result of the hydration break.

Far too much space opens up between Chelsea’s defence and midfield, with Meritti turning and carrying the ball forward. Boga tests Sanchez with a strike from the edge of the box. That was probably Juventus’s most threatening attack.

Palestra defends well as the last man up against Milik, Chelsea almost undone by Locatelli’s outside of the foot pass.

Robert Sanchez caught under a cross swung to the back post, very unconvincing goalkeeping, but Juventus could not get their shot away in the box. Nicoll-Jazuli then did well to bring the ball away for Chelsea at the edge of the box.

Chelsea have another corner, and yet again it comes from a right-sided attack. Chelsea are in ascendancy now after a slow start, but it is a very low intensity contest.

Caicedo with a couple of threatening crosses from a centre-right position, but no Chelsea player can connect with them cleanly. Gittens’s dribbling down the left causing problems for Cambiaso, and he was the one attacking Caicedo’s cross at the back post.

Play has now resumed after the drinks break. No changes from either team, those will come at half time. Chelsea have 21 players sitting on their bench, albeit a number of academy players are on tour.

Time for a hydration break, even though the game is being played under a closed roof.

Chelsea’s right side is their most dangerous, by a distance. Quenda does well to slip Palestra in on the overlap, and his low cross into the six-yard box is cleared for a corner. Juventus clear. Boga with a burst through the Chelsea midfield but the Juventus man then gets his pass wrong.

Kelly with a left-to-right switch to Cambiaso, and his cross deflects off the toe of Miretti in the middle and trickles just wide of the far post. Sanchez was scrambling but I think the goalkeeper had it covered.

Chelsea enjoying their most sustained spell of possession in Juventus’s half so far, without quite carving out a clear cut chance. Juventus defending their penalty area with a back five, but they do not have Bonucci, Chiellini and Barzagli back there anymore.

Quenda with a threatening inswinging cross from the right flank, but Welbeck could not quite rise high enough to direct his header towards the far corner. Quenda was keeping the width for Chelsea with Palestra inside the winger in the box. Quenda then slices a shot over from long range.

Welbeck and Caicedo involved in some good combination play, with Nicoll-Jazuli’s outside of the foot pass finding Gittens. Chelsea’s left-winger runs into traffic, but he has been one of the bright spots of the pre-season campaign thus far.

Having watched a couple of Chelsea’s friendlies, there is a lot to like about Palestra at right-back. Tall, long stride, lots of composure on the ball. Will be interesting to see if they can find a way for him and Reece James to start games. Chelsea as a team yet to find much rhythm in the game so far.

Tosin could well find himself down the pecking order this season among Chelsea’s raft of centre-backs, but he makes an important block in the area before Locatelli drags a shot wide from the edge of the box.

Former Bournemouth defender Lloyd Kelly is in the Juventus team. The Italian team are looking to press high in the early minutes whenever Chelsea try to play out from the back. Quenda with an early dart at the Juventus defence but he gets the pass all wrong with Palestra overlapping.

Palestra with a loose first touch but he recovers and defends well. Like in Sydney, this looks another very bumpy pitch, you can see the join marks between the pieces of turf that have been freshly laid. Coming out of these games without any injuries will be a priority for Alonso.

Juventus get the game started in their pale pink away kit.

Juventus XI: Di Gregorio, Kalulu, Gatti, Kelly, Cambiaso, Douglas Luiz, Locatelli, Miretti, Boga, Milik, Celik

Subs: Perrin, Pinsoglio, Nava, Bremmer, Rugani, Koopmeiners, Arthur Melo, Cabal, Owusu, Gil Puche, Oboavwoduo, Licina, Durmisi, Yildiz, Zhegrova, David

Welbeck starts against Juventus, but no Jordan Henderson with the group just yet. As Sam Dean writes here: “Last season, especially, provided evidence that the balance of their squad was not right, and they are now trying to change the internal dynamic by adding more leadership and experience to the team.”

How long will he stay there? Will he play his way back into Alonso’s team, be shipped out on loan or sold for a fee? Sam Dean assesses the options for player and club in this piece. Out of sight, out of mind could well be the most likely outcome for a player who has missed almost two years of football, and looked extremely raw before his ban.

Looks like a back four once again for Alonso, and Danny Welbeck makes his first Chelsea appearance. Pedro will play off Welbeck as a second striker. Geovany Quenda was signed last year from Sporting CP, but joined up with Chelsea this summer. Another wide forward in their collection.

Chelsea XI: Sanchez; Palestra, Fofana, Tosin, Hato; Caicedo, Nicoll-Jazuli; Quenda, Joao Pedro, Gittens; Welbeck

Chelsea subs: Penders, Sharman-Lowe, Curd, Slonina, Acheampong, Subuloye, Sarr, Diakite, Anselmino, Lavia, Essugo, Watson, Walsh, Kellyman, Mudryk, Estevao Willian, Kavuma-McQueen, Neto, Satpayev, Jackson, Delap

The wheels of commerce continue to turn for Chelsea in the transfer market but this afternoon Xabi Alonso’s team continue their preparations for the new season against Juventus in Hong Kong.

They have the chance to recover from the ignominy of losing to 10-man Tottenham Hotspur in Sydney on Saturday, but with 19 days until Chelsea’s Premier League opener against Fulham these matches are still a fitness building exercise. The positive from the Spurs game was Wesley Fofana, Levi Colwill, Cole Palmer completing 80 minutes – three players who endured injury problems last season.

Another new arrival is expected to follow Morgan Rogers, Marco Palesta, Maxence Lacroix, Jordan Henderson and Danny Welbeck to Stamford Bridge, with the club nearing a deal for Rayo Vallecano left-back Pep Chavarria.

It wouldn’t be Chelsea without talk of some eye-catching outgoings, with Spurs reportedly interested in Nicolas Jackson and Enzo Maresca eyeing a reunion with Pedro Neto at Manchester City.

Alonso’s team promise to be flexible in their tactical approach this season, but so far he has set up with a back four rather than the 3-4-2-1 system he used to such great effect at Bayer Leverkusen. That could change as availability increases closer to the start of the season, but Palestra’s bursts forward from right-back in tandem with Estevao have caught the eye.

Juventus finished sixth in Serie A last season under Luciano Spalletti, the former Roma and Napoli coach who usually guarantees expansive and attractive football. Turkey left-winger Kenan Yildiz was their top goalscorer last season, and it looks like they will make it through the summer without the left-winger being picked off by one of the Premier League’s elite. Yildiz scored 11 goals in all competitions, and Dusan Vlahovic was the only other player to reach double figures so scoring goals is a problem to address. Lois Openda and Randal Kolo Muani have been signed this summer to strengthen the forward line.

#1839. 'He always wanted to play for Scotland'. Alex McLeish recalls the moment the national team found their new talisman in Scott McTominay

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 17:30 EST, 11 November 2026 | Updated: 18:02 EST, 11 November 2026

While Alex McLeish’s second stint as Scotland manager clearly did not go to plan, the compensations from that period proved to be significant for the national team.

Without a struggling side earning a play-off spot in the Nations League, a famous night in Serbia under Steve Clarke would never have been possible.

For all we know, the years in international exile may have rolled on. The ongoing improvement which led to participation at the World Cup this summer might never have happened.

McLeish’s greatest legacy, however, was surely to persuade Scott McTominay to pull on a dark blue shirt after he travelled to Carrington in 2018.

Alerted to the Lancaster-born player’s eligibility by then Manchester United manager Jose Mourinho, the man who won 77 caps for his country could have been forgiven for feeling that the coup he pulled off was just never meant to be.

‘The beast from the east,’ McLeish recalled with a grin.

Scott McTominay (left) and Alex McLeish in 2018 ahead of a friendly against Belgium

McLeish and McTominay together in a Nations League encounter against Albania in 2018

‘When I was forced off the train in Newcastle, they said “it’s not going any further, the weather’s knackered.”

‘So, I had to wait for a train down south. And I thought “at this point will I go home?”

‘And I thought, “no, I’ve come this far, so I’m going all the way”. Then I got to my hotel at five in the morning, the guy says, “oh, I thought you were a no-show, son.”

‘I said - “no - I’ve arrived and I’m needing a room.”

‘I didn’t go in for the breakfast as Mourinho said “just come in at lunchtime, get some food and we’ll have a chat.”

‘But he said he (McTominay) definitely wants to play for Scotland.

‘So, it was good to hear that from Jose.’

Mourinho liked what he saw the minute he set eyes on the player. It’s fair to say that not everyone at the club around that time was similarly enthused.

‘He was still just a kid, quite raw,’ McLeish recalled. ‘But he had the physique, speed and skill on the ball.

‘He was good in the air and also with the ball at his feet. It made it a no-brainer.

‘I’d gone to a couple of Man United games and they were just kind of breeding him into the system.

McTominay in training ahead of the Nations League clash against North Macedonia on Friday

‘Listen, anyone would have done it and brought him into the squad.

‘The only problem we faced was that England were in the frame as well. But when I said to Scott, “I’d love you to play for Scotland,” he said “That’s the only team I want to play for.”

‘And all of a sudden we had a brand new young superstar.’

Truth be told, it would be some time before Scotland supporters began to place McTominay in such a bracket.

He had his moments early on for his country, but his deployment as a defender – by both McLeish and Clarke – did him no favours.

It was only in the qualifiers to Euro 2024 that the futility of that approach was accepted.

McTominay was outstanding as a central midfielder in the qualifiers, his performance and two goals in the famous win against Spain topping the lot.

In little over a year, he’d be a Napoli player. And within a season, he’d become a Serie A winner and voted Italy’s best player.

Many Manchester United fans were outraged that the club had sold him for just £25.7million.

Even some England supporters voiced their displeasure about the player slipping through their hands.

‘They have such a massive pot to pick from in England,’ McLeish reflected.

‘But I’m sure that privately, in some of their chats behind the scenes, they will have said ‘we should have got McTominay.’

‘But he chose Scotland. He wanted to to come. He wasn’t saying anything about England at all.

‘And that was the best news I could have got in that era of rebuild.’

While Clarke rightly got the plaudits for taking the team to three tournaments, McLeish has taken a huge amount of pride from the part McTominay has played in it all.

‘It’s incredible how he’s grown and grown,’ he added.

‘In the first few games, he was just trying to feel his way into the international scene. But he gave everything from that first call-up.

Scott McTominay in action against Haiti in the 2026 World Cup

‘He’s played in just about every position in the team down the years. He was in the back four at one stage.

‘But he’s mainly operated in the middle of the field and he’s a real threat in the box and moving from middle to front.

‘The way he runs with the ball is just superb because he really knows what he’s doing.

‘He’s got massive confidence and I hope that a lot of young Scottish players coming into the game can take inspiration from what Scott has done.'

In a rare media conference this week, McTominay put his underwhelming displays at the World Cup in context.

Two days before the opener against Haiti in Boston, he underwent a controlled electric shock in hospital to restore a normal heart rhythm. Since then, he’s undergone a medical procedure to deal with the arrhythmia.

He returns to the Scotland squad a month after pulling on a Napoli shirt again against Frosinone.

With five goals in his past six matches, it feels like the player the Tartan Army grew to love is back with them.

Sebastien Pocognoli may soon feel he owes McLeish a word of thanks, too.

‘It’ll be a massive relief for the manager to get Scott back into the squad,’ he said.

‘You always want your best players available.

‘I remember back in my day, going to Kazakhstan when we had a lot of boys missing.

‘We were held in a bit of limbo. So, for Sebastien to get players into his team of that level will be massive for him. It could make a huge difference for Scotland.’

#1838. Rwanda vs Mali - prediction, team news, lineups

By Adepoju Marvellous | 15 Nov 2026 12:40, Last updated: 15 Nov 2026 13:17

The top two teams in Group K of the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers face off at Stade Amahoro on Tuesday as Rwanda host Mali.

This is the second meeting between the sides in four days, after Mali edged a 3-2 victory in Bamako last Friday.

Rwanda entered the clash at Stade du 26 Mars on a five-match unbeaten run - four of which were wins - and with the chance to move top of their AFCON qualifying group. They appeared set to do so after goals from Jojea Kwizera and Phanuel Kavita, only for a late collapse to result in a 3-2 defeat.

Beyond missing out on a crucial three points, Stephen Constantine’s men squandered the chance to claim their first victory over Mali in five attempts, a result that would have provided a major psychological boost ahead of the rematch in Kigali.

Amavubi will be eager to return to winning ways and avoid leaving their AFCON hopes in the balance ahead of the final round of qualifiers next March.

Victory on Tuesday could move Rwanda six points clear in the race for a place at the 2027 finals, but defeat could see them slip behind Cape Verde, who are now just behind after their win over Liberia.

Tuesday’s hosts are unbeaten at home since October, keeping clean sheets in three of their last four matches. Another solid defensive display - having never kept a shutout against Mali - would be a key step toward ending their winless run in this fixture.

Like Rwanda, Mali are also in the early stages of a new managerial era, and Anthony da Silva has made an impressive start at the helm - going unbeaten in his first four matches since taking over in June following Tom Saintfiet’s departure.

The most recent of those came against Rwanda last time out, as Les Aigles demonstrated their ability to win matches in different ways by securing their first comeback victory since eliminating 10-man Tunisia at the most recent Africa Cup of Nations.

One of only four teams still boasting a perfect record in the current qualifiers, Mali can move within touching distance of a place at the 2027 AFCON finals, where they will look to extend their run of 10 consecutive tournament appearances dating back to 2008.

Much of that success is due to Mali’s impressive qualifying record, having won five straight and gone 11 matches unbeaten since June 2023 (W9, D2) - a run bettered only by Morocco on the continent in that span.

Not since November 2021 have Tuesday’s visitors won four straight competitive matches, handing them the opportunity to make more history under a manager who has wasted no time stamping his authority on proceedings.

Rwanda Africa Cup of Nations Qualifying form:

Mali Africa Cup of Nations Qualifying form:

Jojea Kwizera was directly involved in both of Rwanda’s goals last time out, and the 27-year-old will be eager to make an impact once again.

Djihad Bizimana has featured in all of his side’s AFCON qualifiers since November 2019 - a streak set to continue on Tuesday.

Ousmane Camara was forced off with an injury late in Mali’s last outing, making the centre-back a doubt for this fixture.

If Camara is unavailable, Cheick Keita could be handed his first competitive start at the heart of the defence.

Lassine Sinayoko has registered five goals and five assists in his last ten appearances for club and country. The Paris FC forward, who set up Moussa Kounfolo Yeo’s equaliser in Bamako, will be aiming to get back on the scoresheet.

Ntwari; Niyomugabo, Kavita, Mutsinzi, Byiringiro; Iradukunda, Bizimana, Ruboneka, Kwizera; Mickels, Biramahire

Diarra; Traore, Camara, Gassama, Guindo; Sangare, Haidara; Yeo, Doumbia, Nene; Sinayoko

As with last week’s encounter, there is little to separate the sides, so another tightly contested match is expected.

Mali’s superior quality proved decisive in the reverse fixture, but we expect Rwanda to claim a point this time and avoid falling six points adrift of their visitors.

#1837. Prediction: USA vs Haiti

The United States head into Tuesday’s second leg of their CONCACAF Nations League quarter-final against Haiti with one foot already in the semi-finals.

After a dominant 6-0 victory in the opening meeting, it would take an extraordinary turnaround for the Americans to be eliminated, as Mauricio Pochettino prepares for his final match in charge before departing for Manchester United.

The USA have little left to do but finish the tie professionally after dismantling Haiti in the first leg.

Tuesday’s match will represent the final game of Mauricio Pochettino’s tenure, and the Argentine will be eager to leave on a high note. While he departs without delivering silverware, he has overseen significant progress since the World Cup, with the United States currently riding a five-match winning streak in all competitions.

The Americans have been particularly impressive in recent months, keeping three consecutive clean sheets and scoring at least three goals in four of their last five matches.

Home form has also been a major strength. The USA have a perfect record in Nations League quarter-final matches on home soil and remain unbeaten at TQL Stadium, where they have won two previous internationals.

History is also firmly on their side. The United States are unbeaten in their last 11 meetings with Haiti and have won the last four encounters by an aggregate score of 10-1.

Julian Hall was the youngest player in the American starting lineup during the first leg, while Santiago Castaneda and Reed Baker-Whiting are still waiting to make their senior international debuts.

Christian Pulisic and Weston McKennie both made their first appearances since the World Cup in the opening match of the tie and immediately made an impact. Pulisic scored twice, while McKennie also found the net.

Hall, Auston Trusty and Folarin Balogun were also on the scoresheet as the Americans ran riot.

Haiti travel to Cincinnati facing a seemingly impossible task after suffering a crushing defeat in the first leg.

David Badia’s side had entered the quarter-finals with momentum after winning their opening three Nations League group-stage matches, but back-to-back defeats have abruptly halted that progress. Their last two losses have come by a combined score of 8-0.

The 6-0 defeat to the USA was particularly painful, marking the first time since 2021 that Haiti had conceded six goals in a single match.

Despite the deficit, Haiti will still be determined to finish the campaign with a positive performance. Their last quarter-final victory in a CONCACAF competition came during the 2019 Gold Cup, when they staged a remarkable comeback from 2-0 down to beat Canada 3-2.

The visitors are also attempting to secure their first victory on American soil against the United States since a World Cup qualifier triumph in 1969.

Goalkeeper Jonah Mednard and midfielder Miguel Joseph remain uncapped at senior international level.

Fabrice Picault is pushing for a place in the starting lineup after beginning the first leg on the bench, while Ruben Providence and Yassin Fortune could also be considered for greater involvement.

With a six-goal advantage already established, the United States can approach this fixture with confidence and relatively little pressure. Pochettino’s side have been in excellent form, while Haiti appear to have lost momentum at exactly the wrong time.

Even if the Americans rotate heavily, the gulf in quality and confidence between the teams should still be evident. Haiti may offer greater resistance than in the first leg, but another comfortable home victory looks the most likely outcome.

#1836. Romano and Moretto provide update on Milan’s Endrick pursuit: “Hasn’t said no”

This week, there have been some interesting rumours about AC Milan and their pursuit of Endrick. However, it may have been a bit misleading.

Yesterday, it seemed that Milan were almost out of the race to sign Endrick, with the Brazilian against the club’s Devil logo. Instead, the Corriere dello Sport report would have you believe that he’d prefer a move to Roma.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

However, his agency have denied this rumour and later reports suggested that the Rossoneri are very much in the race to sign the Brazilian. In fact, he could even leave Real Madrid permanently – with future clauses – so things have certainly developed a bit this week.

Speaking on his YouTube channel today, Romano provided an update on Endrick’s situation alongside Matteo Moretto and their words have been relayed by MilanNews.

“Endrick is currently evaluating his future. On one side, Real Madrid doesn’t want to release him, from the president to Jose Mourinho, who continues to reiterate this publicly; on the other, the boy wants to play,” Romano started.

“I wanted to add a footnote: Endrick’s entourage, ROC Nation, are letting it be known that the player hasn’t said no to Milan; he hasn’t said no to anyone on November 12th. He’s still in the evaluation phase; we’ll see what happens.

“He has two months left with Real Madrid: football changes in five minutes. Endrick’s position is currently completely open, and he’s a player—we were the first to talk about him—that Milan really likes. But it’s true that Roma is also there, there’s a queue of many teams ready to chase him.

“I just wanted to clarify that Endrick hasn’t said no to Milan. He’s keeping everything open while waiting to figure out—if he leaves—the best solution.”

Moretto then added, “A lot will depend on the player. In December, he’ll really understand what kind of path he wants to take. He’s currently noticing this lack of playing time, so the loan option is taking shape. Roma have been maintaining contact for weeks.

“Roma want an additional striker because they believe with one or two signings they can really compete for something important this year. Keep an eye on Roma, but Milan was one of the first to move, and the relationship between Cardinale and ROC Nation is excellent. So far, Roma has maintained contact a little more actively, but Milan is insisting.”

It’s clear that January will be very interesting where Endrick is involved, especially with him being the one to make the decisions on his future.

#1835. Spain vs. England: Three Lions must "worship" Nations League like Cristiano Ronaldo (exclusive)

By Ben Knapton | 15 Nov 2026 13:26

Former England striker Darren Bent, speaking exclusively to Sports Mole, has urged the Three Lions to follow Cristiano Ronaldo's example as they prepare to face Spain in their final UEFA Nations League group-stage fixture.

Thomas Tuchel's men take on the world and European champions in Madrid having already sealed a top-two finish in League A Group 3, guaranteeing progression to the quarter-finals.

Victory for England at the Metropolitano Stadium will also assure the Three Lions of top spot in the group, although a draw or defeat will consign them to a second-placed finish.

Nevertheless, England will compete in the Nations League knockouts for the first time since the 2018-19 edition, as they bid to become just the fourth winners of the tournament after Spain, Portugal and France.

While the Nations League is not held in as high regard as the World Cup or Euros, Bent cannot understand supporters who dismiss the competition as glorified friendlies and points to Ronaldo's passion as an example to follow.

Asked by Sports Mole via MrQ sportsbook how big a chance England have of winning the Nations League if they beat Spain, Bent replied: "Massive chance.

"This is my point: I never understand why certain sections of the fanbase turn their nose up at the Nations League when there's a chance to win a trophy.

"I'd love to win the Euros or the World Cup, but it's incredibly hard to do so. You have to develop a winning mentality and culture throughout your nation.

"If you win the Nations League, look at the pride of Cristiano Ronaldo, someone who has won absolutely everything other than the World Cup, takes in winning every trophy. He worships the Nations League because it's an opportunity for his nation to win something.

"If we can win the Nations League and beat Spain and France along the way, I think that's a massive step forward in terms of where we are as a nation. It would show that we can upset the so-called bigger nations in major competitions.

"It's massive for England to go into that game and beat Spain. They're world champions and European champions. To beat them in the Nations League and go on to win the competition would be huge."

Ronaldo spearheaded Portugal to two Nations League titles in 2019 and 2025, and the five-time Ballon d'Or winner was visibly emotional after the Selecao won the most recent edition.

Ronaldo dropped to his knees as Portugal clinched the crown with victory over Spain on penalties, and he admitted after the game that he could not hold back the waterworks.

"Winning for Portugal is always special. I have many titles with clubs, but nothing is better than winning for Portugal. It's tears. It's duty done and a lot of joy," Ronaldo told SportTV last year.

The 41-year-old may no longer be gracing the international stage with his presence, but England players and fans would do well to heed his words when the Nations League knockouts commence.

#1833. England team news: Thomas Tuchel cuts three players from squad for Spain UEFA Nations League clash

By Darren Plant | 15 Nov 2026 13:43, Last updated: 15 Nov 2026 17:13

Thomas Tuchel has left three players out of his England squad for Sunday's UEFA Nations League fixture against Spain.

The Three Lions make the trip to Madrid needing to beat the world champions to have a chance of finishing top of the group.

Thursday's 2-1 victory over Croatia has put England in that position as they bid to pull off the notable achievement of toppling their long-standing undefeated hosts.

Tuchel has been boosted by the return of Ezri Konsa and Djed Spence, who missed the previous fixture due to fitness issues.

However, that has resulted in a trio of players being omitted from the group for Sunday's pivotal showdown.

Everton defender Jarrad Branthwaite, Toffees midfielder James Garner and Fulham starlet Josh King are the three players to miss out.

Of those players, only Garner earned minutes as a substitute against Croatia.

King had been hoping to make his senior England debut as reward for his eye-catching form in the Premier League.

Instead, he has been allowed to return to club duties alongside the Everton pair.

Tuchel has opted for Konsa, Jarell Quansah, Dan Burn, James Hill and Ben White to be his centre-back options.

While Konsa will almost certainly be recalled to the England XI, it is unclear whether Quansah or Burn will drop out.

Meanwhile, Tuchel appears likely to stick with Trent Alexander-Arnold and Lewis Hall as his full-backs, subsequently leaving Spence to take a place on the substitutes' bench.

#1831. USA pulls out of U-17 World Cup just days before it starts… amid war in the Middle East and 'risk of armed conflict'

Published: 18:48 EST, 11 November 2026 | Updated: 18:48 EST, 11 November 2026

The US Soccer Federation is withdrawing its team from the FIFA U-17 World Cup in Qatar amid growing security concern over the ongoing conflicts in the Middle East, according to multiple reports.

The American State Department currently has a travel advisory for the country at a Level 3, with guidance telling travelers to 'reconsider travel to Qatar due to risk of armed conflict.'

Athletes who were set to compete in the tournament - held from November 19 to December 13 - were informed of the decision via an e-mail.

'We are writing to inform you of the difficult decision to cancel our World Cup pre-camp and our planned participation in the World Cup,' the letter stated.

'We are extremely proud of the preparation by our players and coaches to represent the US in the World Cup.

'Unfortunately, in light of current circumstances including the US State Department's Level 3 Travel Advisory for Qatar and related directives for Embassy staff and families, we are no longer able to participate in the tournament. The well-being of our players and staff will always be our top priority.'

The United States has told players they will not participate in the FIFA U-17 World Cup in Qatar

The US State Department has a Level 3 travel advisory for the country amid ongoing conflicts

The USA won their CONCACAF qualifying group in order to reach the tournament

This announcement comes one week after coach Alex Aldaz announced his roster for the competition. The team was set to take part in a training camp this week at US Soccer's new headquarters outside Atlanta.

Players were set to open their tournament on November 21 with a match against Montenegro. They were also scheduled to face Chile and Algeria.

The United States earned the right to compete in the tournament by winning their group and outlasting the Dominican Republic on goal difference in CONCACAF U-17 World Cup qualifying.

The Baby Nats drew the Dominicans after beating Saint Kitts and Nevis as well as Saint Vincent and the Grenadines.

At last year's tournament, the Americans reached the Round of 32 before being eliminated by Morocco.

The best finish for the United states at the tournament came in New Zealand in 1999, when they came fourth - losing to Australia on penalties. Landon Donovan was named as the competition's Best Player.

FIFA made changes to the tournament last year, making it an annual event rather than once every two years. Qatar won the rights to host it from 2025 to 2029.

It is not clear which team will replace the United States at the tournament. The Daily Mail has contacted FIFA for comment on the matter.

#1830. ​Arteta’s ‘dynasty’ dream collides with Arsenal’s harsh reality

Mikel Arteta says he wants to create a “dynasty” at Arsenal as he threw down the gauntlet to his players to retain their Premier League title and reach a “different level”.

Arsenal are on the verge of completing a £75m deal for Brazil midfielder Bruno Guimãraes from Newcastle and have not given up hope of landing Real Madrid winger Vinícius Júnior, who has been offered an improved contract by the Spanish giants.

The Premier League champions slumped to a 3-1 defeat to Real Betis in Dublin on Wednesday night, when they paid the price for individual errors and a lethargic, sloppy defensive display.

But that did little to quell Arteta’s ambitions for the new season. “I’m even more excited [about this season], and we’re going to go and attack every possible title because that’s the ambition that we have,” he said.

“We know that we have the ability. We will go from a strength to a strength as well, whether it’s with the players that we have to take them to a different level, and with the market that is still open to recruit as well, so we are very optimistic about it.

“All the work that we’ve done – that I’ve done through the summer – is to understand what we need to do to win again and to create a dynasty in this football club. That’s the aim.”

Despite Arteta’s bullishness, he conceded Arsenal would have to be a lot better than they were against Betis. When asked about the mood in the dressing room, he said: “Very upset, given a hard time. They are fuming, but this is good. That’s what we need.”

Telegraph Sport analyses some of the talking points from a disappointing evening at the Aviva Stadium.

The importance of goalkeeper David Raya and centre-backs William Saliba and Gabriel Magalhães to Arsenal hardly needs overstating. Their title success was built on the foundations provided by that triumvirate at the back.

Raya has yet to report back from holiday after Spain’s World Cup triumph and Saliba is facing an extended spell on the sidelines with a back injury. Gabriel did appear for the second half but, watching this, Arteta is unlikely to have been dissuaded from the belief he needs another top defender to compensate for the loss of Saliba.

It may have been only Arsenal’s second game of pre-season, so a degree of legginess was understandable.

But the ease with which they were cut open and overloaded by the Spanish side, and the volume of individual errors, did not sit comfortably with Arteta with just over a fortnight until they kick off their title defence at home to newly promoted Coventry City.

Only once in 63 matches last season did Arsenal concede three goals in a single game but they were fortunate Betis did not score more. “In the first half there are two different things: to play well and to compete,” said Arteta, who saw his side trail 3-1 at the interval.

“We did the first one quite well in a lot of moments but the compete part – especially in and around our box – was not to the standards to win a football match against a good side. It’s better to give them [the goals away] in a friendly match than an official match. It’s always good when you lose a match in pre-season because it creates a bit more fire in the belly.”

Kepa Arrizabalaga will not want to watch Betis’s first goal back in a hurry. The Arsenal goalkeeper may have got a slight nudge as he came for the ball at a corner but he was all over the place and never looked even in the vaguest control of the situation. Rodrigo Riquelme scored at the far post after the ball sailed over the keeper. Arteta called it a “really sloppy goal”. With former Leeds goalkeeper Illan Meslier having arrived on a free transfer as back-up to Raya, Kepa faces an uncertain future at Arsenal. Moments like this will not help his cause.

He did not feature much last season but is probably best remembered for his torrid showing in the Carabao Cup final defeat by Manchester City in March. He looked as unconvincing here as he did then, as the former Chelsea goalkeeper also sliced a clearance in the build up to Betis’s third goal. Before then, Kai Havertz had turned over possession cheaply from which Nelson Deossa set up former West Ham midfielder Pablo Fornals to score.

Arsenal need more creativity and firepower in attack, hence the interest in Vinícius and Atlético Madrid’s Julián Alvarez. Viktor Gyokeres again looked rather limited here and the likes of Bukayo Saka and Eberechi Eze are also still to report back. Yet one of the few, brighter aspects of Arsenal’s performances was the sight of the regal looking Riccardo Calafiori marauding forward from a very nominal left-back role.

If Arsenal are going to play more adventurously this season and try to ratchet up things in the entertainment stakes then Calafiori could have a big role to play, as long as Arteta can keep him fit. He can be a potent weapon galloping forward and there were clear glimpses of that here. Harnessing that talent while not compromising too much defensive security may be one of the manager’s challenges.

Louie Copley had only been on the pitch for nine minutes – a half-time substitute for Ben White – when the 19-year-old midfielder went down largely unchallenged with what looked like a troubling knee injury. Arteta admitted afterwards that the way the teenager fell to the ground was a concern and he looked in visible pain and distress as he was treated by the medical staff before being helped off the pitch.

The fear will be of some kind of ligament damage and Arteta confirmed Copley would be scanned on Thursday. “Quite worried to be fair for the kid because the mechanism doesn’t look very positive and the symptoms that he already has,” the manager said. “So we are going to have to wait and see for tomorrow’s scan. Touch wood that is not a bad one.”

Premier League champions Arsenal continue their preparations for the new season as they take on Spanish side Real Betis at the Aviva Stadium in Dublin, with this being the first-ever meeting between the two sides. This is the first time Arsenal have played a pre-season game in Dublin since August 2018, when they drew 1-1 with London rivals Chelsea, with Arsenal winning on penalties.

Arsenal beat Girona 4-1 in their opening game of pre-season, with new signing Christos Tzolis on the scoresheet in his first appearance for the club. After today, Arsenal have three more games, including the Community Shield, before they kick off the defence of their Premier League crown at home against newly-promoted Coventry on opening night of the new season. They are closing in on a deal for Newcastle captain Bruno Guimaraes, who is set to become one of Arsenal’s most expensive signings. Mikel Arteta’s side have been dealt a blow ahead of the season with the news that France centre-back William Saliba will miss an extended period due to a back injury. The likes of Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Noni Madueke are still yet to return after their World Cup exploits.

Real Betis, under the management of former Manchester City boss Manuel Pellegrini, finished fifth in La Liga last season and have therefore qualified for this coming season’s Champions League after a 20-year absence from the competition. #1827. Pochettino dismisses distraction fears ahead of USMNT farewell

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Mauricio Pochettino insisted his full focus remained on the United States ahead of his final match in charge before departing for Manchester United.

Pochettino was confirmed as Man Utd's new head coach last week after Michael Carrick was sacked, with the Red Devils languishing in the Premier League relegation zone.

The Argentine signed a contract with the USA until 2030 in August after reaching the round of 16 at the World Cup.

It was confirmed that Pochettino would take charge of the Stars and Stripes' CONCACAF Nations League quarter-final against Haiti before heading to Manchester, with the USA winning the first leg 6-0.

Pochettino's decision to remain in charge has been criticised, but he insisted there was no conflict of interest ahead of the second leg at FC Cincinnati's TQL Stadium.

"For me, it's not difficult. I think we ​are well-prepared to switch quickly – like a player, from the national team to the clubs," Pochettino told reporters.

"From one game that you don't play well to another that you need to be ​ready again. From one action to the next action.

"The business is to be focused here ‌for ⁠the game against Haiti. But for sure, in the moment that [we] finish, we are going to start to be 100% focused on our next project."

Mauricio Pochettino speaks to the media in Cincinnati ahead of our @CNationsLeague second leg match against Haiti. LIVE NOW: https://t.co/Tm5hNWPyMF https://t.co/sykam13DEd

— U.S. Soccer Men's National Team (@USMNT) November 16, 2026

Pochettino returns to the Premier League two years on from being sacked at Chelsea, with United the fourth different team he has managed in England during his career.

He had been linked with a move to Old Trafford back in 2022, but United instead opted to appoint Erik ten Hag.

Pochettino is United's eighth permanent boss since the retirement of Alex Ferguson in May 2013, and he put pen to paper on a two-and-a-half-year deal.

During his time at Tottenham, Pochettino oversaw the most Premier League games in the club's history and recorded the most wins (113), while also leading Spurs to the Champions League final in 2019, in which they were beaten 2-0 by Liverpool.

And Liverpool will be Pochettino's first opponents when he sits in the United dugout for the first time on Sunday.

Pochettino is expected to land in England on Thursday, but he confirmed members of his coaching staff will already be there when he arrives.

"That was the ⁠plan when ​we agreed terms with Manchester United and ​with the national team," Pochettino added.

"They are preparing everything there because on Wednesday, when we arrive, it's ​going to be non-stop."

#1826. Gomes scores for Aston Villa in defeat by Bayern Munich in Hong Kong

Aston Villa’s tour of the Far East ended in defeat as they lost 2-1 to German champions Bayern Munich in a pre-season friendly at the Kai Tak Sports Park in Hong Kong on Friday.

Bayern took the lead inside the final 10 minutes of the first half, with defender Kim Min-jae heading in from Tom Bischof’s sublime free-kick. Villa goalkeeper Marco Bizot made a string of saves in the second half to keep Bayern’s lead at one goal until former Liverpool forward Luis Díaz smashed in Bayern’s second off the underside of the bar.

Just as the game appeared to be out of reach for Aston Villa, who had struggled to create much going forward for most of the game, Unai Emery’s side showed some life late on. Summer signing João Gomes’s goal from the edge of the box gave them hope before Tammy Abraham nearly brought them back onto level terms, only to be denied by a fine save from 40-year-old Manuel Neuer.

Aston Villa are next in action in six days’ time when they take on Paris St-Germain in the Uefa Super Cup before kicking off their Premier League campaign at Brighton. Bayern have one more friendly to come against RB Leipzig before the DFL-Supercup against Borussia Dortmund. They then kick off the defence of their Bundesliga crown against Stuttgart at home on August 28.

Stepping up in the big moments! 🐐🧤 pic.twitter.com/r14rF39XpR

Unai Emery’s men head home from the Far East to face PSG in the Uefa Super Cup in Salzburg next week and then have one more pre-season friendly against Borussia Monchengladbach before starting their Premier League campaign at Brighton.

Possession: Aston Villa 44%-56% Bayern MunichShots: 8-16Shots on target: 3-8Corners: 3-7

Bizot nearly has a calamitous moment coming out of his penalty area but gets away with it.

The final whistle is blown soon after and Bayern hold on to beat Villa 2-1 in Hong Kong. They had looked comfortable when Diaz put them 2-0 up but Villa kept going until the end.

Victory in the final match of the #AudiFCBTour! 💪🔥 pic.twitter.com/UFhQhme62i

The space opens up for Palhinha to shoot from range but Bizot makes a fairly comfortable save down to his right.

It was all Bayern for 80 minutes of this game but Villa have come to life in the closing stages, with Vincent Kompany’s side now holding on a bit.

When Diaz scored Bayern’s second goal, Aston Villa were out of this game but it has been all Villa since then. They look the more likely to get a goal.

Gomes’ free-kick out on the left is parried behind by Neuer for a Villa corner on the right. The corner comes to nothing.

For 80 minutes, Aston Villa barely looked like scoring but come so close to getting two goals in just a few minutes. Abraham meets a cross from the right and must think he has scored but his header is brilliantly saved by the 40-year-old Neuer.

Maybe this game is not quite done and dusted yet. A cross from the right picks out Gomes on the edge of the box. The Brazilian takes one touch before toe poking past Neuer and into the Bayern net. Gomes meant that finish and Villa have some hope.

Abraham should have done better there. He has the space to drive down Villa’s right and has a decision to make; cross the ball to his left and drive forward himself to shoot. He takes a while to make the decision before his attempted cross is intercepted by Ito.

Boey’s yellow card was his final act of the game as he is replaced by Della Rovere. Boey did seem to be struggling with some cramp.

Bayern receive their second yellow card of the game as Boey is booked for cynically pulling down Lynch.

Cash, Maatsen and Buendia have gone off for Aston Villa.

Double substitution from Bayern as Pavic and Assomo replace Tah and Brown.

A fantastic goal to put the Germans 2-0 up and it is nothing more than they deserve. Ibrahimovic finds Diaz in space on the left and the Colombian drives at Cash. As he enters the Villa box, Diaz cuts inside onto his preferred right foot and smashes a shot towards goal. It appeared to go right over Bizot, who opts not to put a hand up. The ball crashes off the underside of the bar and goes in. It has been all Bayern in this second half and that goal had been coming.

Bayern are knocking on the door and come very close to doubling their lead. Diaz’s shot from the edge of the box looks destined to hit the net with Bizot beaten but fortunately for Villa Abraham is on hand on his own goal line to make the block.

Bizot makes another great save. Bayern win a free-kick out on the right after Brown was fouled. Bischoff opts to shoot instead of crossing and nearly beats Bizot at his near post but the Aston Villa keeper gets across to his left to make the save.

Unai Emery makes a double substitution as Mings and Lynch replace Torres and Guessand. Mings takes the captain’s armband.

That is a fantastic double save from Bizot, first denying Stanisic and then Ibrahimovic. Both of those shots came through bodies so Bizot did a good job of reacting and making the saves with his legs on both occasions.

It is safe to say the Bayern fans out in Hong Kong love Diaz, who is cheered every time he touches the ball.

Vincent Kompany is going to make a triple change as Ito, Diaz and Palhinha come on. Former Liverpool man Diaz received a great ovation from the fans in Hong Kong. Palhinha, who spent last season on loan at Tottenha, has been linked with a move to Aston Villa in this window.

Should Bayern have been awarded a penalty there? A ball is played in behind the Villa defence into the penalty area and Ibrahimovic appeared to be brought down but the referee waves those appeals away. On first viewing, that appeared to be a penalty.

Just before the hour mark, it is time for some changes from Aston Villa. Abraham and Bogarde come on for Madjo and Kamara. This is Abraham’s first appearance of this pre-season.

Good play from Gomes earns Aston Villa a free-kick not far outside the Bayern penalty area out on the left, in a similar position to the free-kick that Bayern scored from in the first half. Buendia clips in a good ball to the back post, where Guessand looks likely to score but instead misses the ball on the stretch. Should Guessand have done better with that? Probably.

Brown was starting in his customary left-back position for Bayern in the first half but is now operating out on the right wing.

Gomes leaves one late on Pavlovic and, had this been a competitive fixture, I suspect that might have been a yellow card.

Tah is brought down by Gomes and Bayern will have a free-kick out on the right not a million miles outside the Villa penalty area. The delivery though is poor and easily cleared away.

Bayern have brought Stanisic on at half-time for Laimer. Aston Villa have not made a change at the break.

Possession: Aston Villa 45%-55% Bayern MunichShots: 4-7Shots on target: 1-2Corners: 1-2

The first half in Hong Kong is brought to an end and Bayern take a 1-0 lead into the break courtesy of Kim’s goal.

There will be one added minute at the end of this first half.

Aston Villa have struggled to create much going forward and have not really had a genuine goal-scoring opportunity in this first half. Their forward line though will look quite different when they kick off the seaosn than it does today.

The German side take the lead in Hong Kong. Bischof’s left-footed delivery from a free-kick out on the left is sublime, whipping it right into the corridor of uncertainty. The quality of delivery means it is quite a simple header for Kim, who makes no mistake with his header into the far corner. Kim might have been offside but obviously there is no VAR in use today. 1-0 Bayern.

That is a waste in the end from Bayern. Boey fires a pass in-field into Laimer, who takes a fantastic first touch on the turn inside the Villa half. He drives through the Villa half and at the penalty area but his pass outside looking for Cardozo is poor and overhit, with the ball rolling out for a goal kick. Laimer will be annoyed at himself having done all the hard work and then failed to execute the easy part.

Bischof eyes one up from range and tries to pick out the top corner. Bizot is routed to his spot and is hoping the shot goes wide. Bischof’s effort is always curling wide, much to Bizot’s relief.

The first booking of the game goes the way of Bayern Munich. Guessand drives forward into the Bayern half and is brought down by a cynical foul from Cardozo. You were half expecting Cardozo to perhaps escape without a booking with it being a pre-season friendly but he does not. It was the right call to book him.

That was lovely from Pavlovic. The German midfielder shows good feet to beat Gomes before getting his shot away from a central position just outside the box. He forces Bizot into a decent save but one he should be making.

Bayern force Villa into an error and win themselves a corner as a result out on the left. It is delivered into a dangerous area at the front post but Villa do a good job of handling it and clearing their lines.

Bayern Munich have made two signings this summer; Brown from Bundesliga rivals Frankfurt and Saibari from PSV. Brown is starting at left-back for Bayern today with Saibari not involved as he closes in on a return from a knock picked up at the World Cup with Morocco. Brown feels like such a Bayern signing, nabbing a good player from a Bundesliga rival.

Aston Villa have made four signings so far this summer but just one is in their starting XI today in the form of Gomes, who joined from Midlands rivals Wolves this summer. Young Swiss midfielder Manzambi has joined from Freiburg but is currently out injured. Garnacho picked up a knock and Cisse, who has arrived from LASK, is not involved for Villa today.

The ball is played in behind the Aston Villa defence to pick out the run of Binder. On the edge of the Villa box, Binder gets the first touch but Lindelof is calm in defence and heads back to his keeper Bizot.

Moments later, Gomes is dispossessed inside his own half and Ibrahimovic has a shot from just outside the box but drags it wide of the far post.

Good work from 17-year-old Madjo down Aston Villa’s left wins them their first corner of the game. Buendia’s inswinger is headed away too easily at the near post. Aston Villa have seen their former set-piece coach Austin MacPhee nabbed this summer by Xabi Alonso’s Chelsea.

The referee is allowing the game to flow and thus not blowing for soft fouls.

The first chance of the game falls to Bayern Munich. Brown’s cross from the left is headed by Maatsen straight to Ibrahimovic on the edge of the box. Ibrahimovic, not any relation to Zlatan, takes the shot on first time but it is blocked by Maatsen, who makes up for that poor header with the block. The ball goes behind for a corner, which comes to nothing.

Interestingly, there are only eight outfield substitutions on the Aston Villa bench for this game, with the likes of Garnacho and McGinn picking up knocks the other day. It appears then that at least a couple of Villa outfield players will have to play the full 90.

Both sides emerge from the tunnel, Aston Villa led out by Matty Cash and Bayern Munich by Manuel Neuer, and we are closing in on kick-off in Hong Kong. A group of delegates shake the hands of both starting XIs.

Chelsea and Juventus played in this stadium the other night and it is safe to say that the pitch does not look in the best state ahead of kick-off today. It looks like it will continue to rip up and the last thing the two managers will want is to pick up any serious injuries.

Currently, before the two sides emerge, the crowd in Hong Kong are being treated to some pre-match dancing and entertainment, which includes people dressed as pandas and sharks dancing. Would the Premier League ever take inspiration and have dancing pandas before kick-off?

Aston Villa: Bizot, Cash, Lindelof, Torres, Maatsen, Kamara, Joao Gomes, Hemmings, Buendia, Guessand, Madjo.Substitutes: Wright, Asemota, Mings, Abraham, Nedejkovic, Bogarde, Rowe, Burrowes, Carroll, Lynch.

Bayern Munich: Neuer, Kim, Tah, Brown, Boey, Laimer, Bischof, Pavlovic, Ibrahimovic, Binder, Cardozo. Substitutes: Ulrich, Podar-Stiube, Urbig, Kimmich, Luis Díaz, Palhinha, Ito, Chávez, Pavic, Bara, Manuba, Stanisic, Della Rovere, Assomo.

The likes of Ollie Watkins, Ezri Konsa and Emi Martinez are yet to return to training after their World Cup exploits and Aston Villa are also without captain John McGinn and new signing Alejandro Garnacho, who picked up knocks in their win over BG Pathum the other day.

Aston Villa have already sold Youri Tielemans and Morgan Rogers this summer, with Lucas Digne on the verge of a move to PSG, but could another starter be on the way out of Villa Park? England defender Ezri Konsa has been linked with moves to the likes of Arsenal and Liverpool but will Unai Emery be able to keep hold of the 28-year-old?

It has been a big summer of change at Aston Villa already and there could be more changes before the end of the window. Left-back Lucas Digne is set to move to PSG and is set to be replaced by Atlético Madrid’s Matteo Ruggeri. Joao Palhinha, who is on the bench for Bayern Munich today, has been linked with a move to Aston Villa.

“Aston Villa are a top side with a very good coach. They have a large squad and will field plenty of talent. They have already played more friendlies than us, but for us it is a good challenge. It is a match in which we will learn a lot about our team’s fitness. It will be a good match for us.”

Aston Villa’s preparations for the new season continue out in Hong Kong as they take on Bundesliga champions Bayern Munich at the Kai Tak Stadium. These sides have met twice before; Aston Villa beat Bayern 1-0 to win the European Cup in 1981/82 before then meeting in the Champions League group stages during the 2024/25 season, with Jhon Duran’s long-range screamer giving Aston Villa a 1-0 win at Villa Park.

After losing two of their first three pre-season friendlies, Aston Villa have won their first two games on Asian soil and this game marks the end of their tour of the Far East. It has been a summer of significant change at Aston Villa thus far with some key members of their squad departing and some new faces arriving. Youri Tielemans has departed after Manchester United triggered his release clause and they then sold Morgan Rogers to Chelsea for a British transfer record £117m. Unai Emery’s side have brought in 20-year-old Swiss midfielder Johan Manzambi, Brazilian midfielder Joao Gomes and Alejandro Garnacho, with the deal for Garnacho being an initial loan. Manzambi is currently on the sidelines due to a knee injury.

Unai Emery’s side were dealt a blow during the World Cup as Belgian midfielder Amadou Onana picked up a serious knee injury. They were though boosted by the return of Boubacar Kamara after seven months out as he scored in the 3-1 friendly victory over BG Parthum. As one midfielder returned from injury in that game, another picked up a fresh injury as John McGinn suffered a knock to his knee. The likes of Ollie Watkins, Ezri Konsa and Emi Martinez are yet to return after their world Cup exploits. They begin their Premier League campaign with an away game on the south coast against Brighton on August 23 but will be involved in the Uefa Super Cup against PSG next week having lifted the Europa League last season.

Bayern Munich head into this season looking to win a third straight Bundesliga title and have won two of their three friendlies, losing once. They have added Moroccan attacker Ismael Saibari from PSV and German left-back Nathaniel Brown from Bundesliga rivals Eintracht Frankfurt to their ranks this summer. The likes of Harry Kane, Dayot Upamecano and Michael Olise are not available as they are still yet to return after World Cup duty but Vincent Kompany has confirmed that Bayern’s German stars are set to return.

After today, Bayern have one more friendly against RB Leipzig before the DFL-Supercup against Borussia Dortmund. They then kick off the defence of their Bundesliga crown against Stuttgart at home on August 28.

#1824. CF: Instalments and repeatable bonuses – the exact figure Milan paid for Goncalo Ramos

Today, more information about the structure and cost of Goncalo Ramos’ move to AC Milan has been revealed.

It’s fair to say that Ramos’ start to life with Milan has been poor. The Portuguese striker has not scored (or assisted) as many as had been hoped from a player worth a substantial amount and it’s fair to suggest that some have been disappointed with his time at San Siro so far.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

However, the club will not be giving up on him anytime soon, considering he is their record arrival.

This evening, Calcio e Finanza have looked at the fee paid for Ramos – as they did for Diego Moreira recently – and picked apart both the fee, the bonuses and the structure of the payment, as MilanNews relays.

In terms of the fixed fee, the Rossoneri agreed on a deal worth €70 million, with an extra €3.1m in additional costs. This figure will be paid over the course of four years, with yearly payments scheduled on July 15 on each year – ending in July 2029 – and each payment will be worth €17.5m.

Then, there is €16m in bonuses that can be achieved, taking the total fee to almost €90m if all bonuses are achieved.

If Milan win the Scudetto, €2m will be owed; then there are several Champions League bonuses, which could be worth up to €5.2m if the Diavolo win the competition. Finally, if he is the top goalscorer in Serie A, another €2m will be owed to PSG.

These bonuses are capped at €16m and are repeatable, but they’ll only be redeemable if the Portuguese plays 60% of games in that season, unless he is the top scorer, where only the €2m will be owed.
